options.name: -c
options.description: Execute the Python code in command. command can be one or more statements separated by newlines, with significant leading whitespace as in normal module code

options.name: -m
options.description: Search sys.path for the named module and execute its contents as the __main__ module

options.name: -h
options.description: Print a short description of all command line options

options.name: --help
options.description: Print a short description of all command line options

options.name: -V
options.description: Print the Python version number and exit

options.name: --version
options.description: Print the Python version number and exit

options.name: -b
options.description: Issue a warning when comparing bytes or bytearray with str or bytes with int. Issue an error when the option is given twice (-bb)

options.name: -B
options.description: If given, Python won’t try to write .pyc files on the import of source modules

options.name: --check-hash-based-pycs
options.description: Control the validation behavior of hash-based .pyc files. See Cached bytecode invalidation

options.name: -d
options.description: Turn on parser debugging output (for expert only, depending on compilation options)

options.name: -E
options.description: Ignore all PYTHON* environment variables, e.g. PYTHONPATH and PYTHONHOME, that might be set

options.name: -i
options.description: When a script is passed as first argument or the -c option is used, enter interactive mode after executing the script or the command, even when sys.stdin does not appear to be a terminal

options.name: -I
options.description: Run Python in isolated mode. This also implies -E and -s. In isolated mode sys.path contains neither the script’s directory nor the user’s site-packages directory

options.name: -O
options.description: Remove assert statements and any code conditional on the value of __debug__

options.name: -OO
options.description: Do -O and also discard docstrings

options.name: -g
options.description: Don’t display the copyright and version messages even in interactive mode

options.name: -R
options.description: Turn on hash randomization. This option only has an effect if the PYTHONHASHSEED environment variable is set to 0, since hash randomization is enabled by default

options.name: -s
options.description: Don’t add the user site-packages directory to sys.path

options.name: -S
options.description: Disable the import of the module site and the site-dependent manipulations of sys.path that it entails

options.name: -u
options.description: Force the stdout and stderr streams to be unbuffered. This option has no effect on the stdin stream

options.name: -v
options.description: Print a message each time a module is initialized, showing the place (filename or built-in module) from which it is loaded

options.name: -W
options.description: Warning control. Python’s warning machinery by default prints warning messages to sys.stderr

options.name: -x
options.description: Skip the first line of the source, allowing use of non-Unix forms of #!cmd. This is intended for a DOS specific hack only

options.name: -X
options.description: Reserved for various implementation-specific options
